summary: Anne Nishimura Morse works in Japanology, history, and archaeology. She studied under Taka Yanagisawa, Yutaka Hirata, and doctoral supervisor John M. Rosenfield, later holding visiting posts at Tokyo National Research Institute (1988), Nara National Museum (1996), and Kyoto National Museum (1998).

Anne Ruth Hansen specializes in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology, having studied under Charles Hallisey. She was affiliated with the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee (attested 2007) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison as Associate Professor (attested 2012) and Professor of History (attested 2026).
Anne-Marie Blondeau is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies who studied under Rolf Alfred Stein. She held an academic post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études.
Annegret Bollée was a linguist who studied at the University of Hamburg around 1957, Aix-Marseille University, and the University of Bonn in 1969.

Annemarie Schimmel worked in religious studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology, earning doctorates at Berlin and Marburg under Hans Ellenberg, Hans Heinrich Schaeder, and Friedrich Heiler. She held professorships at Marburg, Ankara University (1954–1967), and Harvard University (1967–1992).

Annemarie von Gabain specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (around 1923–1930), later teaching there (around 1938–1945) before serving as a professor at the University of Hamburg (around 1950–1966).

Annette Baier was a philosopher who completed degrees at the University of Otago and a PhD at Somerville College, Oxford. She taught at Carnegie Mellon University (around 1969–1973) and in the philosophy department at the University of Pittsburgh (around 1973–1995).

Annette L. Heitmann specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Christian Lindtner and David Seyfort Ruegg, and attended the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (1987–1989) before earning her doctoral degree at the University of Vienna by 2002.

Annette Schmiedchen works in Indology, history, and archaeology. She earned her PhD at Humboldt University of Berlin and completed her Habilitation at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, where she was a faculty member (around 1999–2014) before researching at Humboldt around 2014.

Annie Besant worked in religious studies and Indology, studying at Birkbeck, University of London around 1879–1883. She founded Banaras Hindu University in 1898, serving as its President, and served as President of the Theosophical Society from around 1907 to 1933.

Anthony C. Yu was a scholar of sinology and religious studies who studied at Houghton University, Fuller Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago (PhD around 1963–1969). He spent his career at the University of Chicago from around 1968 to 2005.

Anthony Cerulli works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Chicago from around 2000 to 2007 and served at the University of Wisconsin-Madison around 2014 as Professor of South Asian Studies and Director of Graduate Studies.

Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé was a sinologist and historian who studied at Leiden University under Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak in 1928. He became a lecturer in Chinese at Leiden in 1946 and served as Professor from 1956 to 1975.

Anthony Tribe works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Bristol and completed a DPhil at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, Steven Collins, and Paul Williams. He held posts at the University of Montana and University of Arizona.

Antoine Cabaton worked in linguistics, history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales and the École du Louvre, and later held a post at the Bibliothèque nationale de France from around 1899 to 1928.
Antoine Lutz completed his PhD at Pierre and Marie Curie University, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Francisco J. Varela.

Antoine Meillet was a linguist specializing in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated in Paris under Ferdinand de Saussure, James Darmesteter, and Sylvain Lévi, he taught at INALCO and held chairs at the EPHE and Collège de France (1905–1936).

Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy was a linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He held chairs in Arabic and Persian at INALCO, was Professor of Persian at Collège de France (1806–1838), and founded and presided over the Société Asiatique.
Antoine-Louis Henri de Polier was an Indologist who studied under traditional teacher Ramachandra Vidyalankara and served as a Colonel in the East India Company.

Antoine-Léonard de Chézy was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy and Louis-Mathieu Langlès. He worked at the Bibliothèque nationale de France and held the chair of Sanskrit at the Collège de France from 1815 to 1832.
